rows.why: Item 10 asks how each step's keyword and text are recorded. Its pick keeps the keyword as written (And, But and * are not resolved) and trims the text after the keyword. That is what S1 expects: the keyword as written and the text after the keyword and one space.

Item 7 asks what happens to the description text under 'Feature:', which is the one rule in S2 that is not obvious. Its pick drops non-step lines before the first Scenario or Background without error, which matches S2 skipping them. Items 11 (tags attach to the next scenario) and 12 (comments and blank lines skipped) cover S2's other clauses, and their picks also agree.
No item asks whether background steps are returned on their own or copied into each scenario. Item 6 is about a Background placed after a Scenario or repeated, which is different behaviour.

Item 9 asks how doc strings and tables attach to steps. Its pick strips indentation to the opening delimiter's indent and trims table cells, as S4 expects. Item 12 adds that lines inside a doc string are kept verbatim, which fits S4's rule that they are never read as keywords, comments or tags.

S5 is about which line each error reports. Item 4 asks exactly that for an unclosed doc string, and its pick (the line that opened it) matches. Items 2 and 3 touch other clauses. Item 3 (Outline rejected as not supported) agrees. Item 2 always reports line 1, while S5 expects the first line of content, so it would differ if comments or blank lines come before that content.
Item 1 asks what happens when the file has no scenarios. Its pick returns the feature with an empty scenarios list instead of raising an error, which is what S6 expects.
